clue.text: Gunners' stunner is a tangy tidbit

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: An artillery regiment's glamorous mascot is described as a tangy little treat.
explanation.walkthrough: RA plus DISH gives RADISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a small peppery root vegetable eaten raw as a sharp-tasting snack or salad morsel.

clue.text: Blew the lights again, but didn't jump

blocks.note: first meaning: ..., blew a fuse once more
second meaning: balked, as a horse at a fence

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as RE-FUSED: fused again. The second is a horse refusing a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that refuses stops short at an obstacle, and fusing again means a blown fuse, both from one spelling.

clue.text: Snuff it without starting to record Grateful Dead's music

indicators.note: starting means the opening letters of the following words
without in its old sense means outside, so one part wraps the other

blocks.note: to snuff it is to die
opening letter of record
opening letter of Grateful

explanation.surface: A deadhead hopes to record the Grateful Dead before dying.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE around R and G gives DIRGE. The Grateful Dead are a rock band, but 'Dead's music' is music for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a lament sung at a funeral, so it is music for those who have died.

clue.text: 8 gives way to ancient scribe's equipment

indicators.note: to here means added on, so the following part comes next

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for street, a way
an inkhorn was a horn container for ink carried by scribes

explanation.surface: Something gives way under an old scribe's writing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives way' is a phrase in the surface, but 'gives' links and 'way' is ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinkhorn is a foul-smelling woodland mushroom, so it is a kind of fungus, the answer to 8.

clue.text: Mocking figure on top of sea chest

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across light is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept
sitting on something places one part directly against the next in the line

blocks.note: the first letter of sea
a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: A grinning figurehead is carved on the lid of a sailor's sea chest.
explanation.walkthrough: S then COFFER gives SCOFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scoffs jeers and derides, so a scoffer is a person given to ridicule.

clue.text: Feature of 6 carrying a measure of itself

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

blocks.note: a star is a feature of the firmament, the answer to 6
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A sky feature holds a measure of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: STAR holds ELL to give STELLAR. 'Itself' points back to the star, so the definition means 'of a star'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means relating to the stars, so it describes what belongs to a star.

clue.text: Go round with gold piece

indicators.note: with adds one part alongside the next

blocks.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Pass a gold coin around the circle.
explanation.walkthrough: OR plus BIT gives ORBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to circle around something, as a moon travels around a planet.

clue.text: Definite agreement takes time in Heaven

indicators.note: takes means adds on, so the following part comes after

blocks.note: firm means definite, as in a firm offer
amen expresses agreement
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A firm accord takes time to reach in the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRM + AMEN + T gives FIRMAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, the heavens arching above the earth.

clue.text: What's in spots? The same old story

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other

blocks.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
eh is a request for repetition, 'what?'

explanation.surface: A doctor asks what's in the spots, hearing the familiar tale again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' is 'what' with 's for 'is': the exclamation of puzzlement sits inside the outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material presented again with little change, a recycled tale.

clue.text: Growth of Manchu students carrying little weight

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside

blocks.note: Fu Manchu is the fictional villain
the National Union of Students
g is the abbreviation for gram

explanation.surface: Fu Manchu's students carry a bit of weight to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: FU then NUS carrying G: FU + N(G)US gives FUNGUS. The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus is an organism that grows as mould or mushroom, so it is an outgrowth.

clue.text: Pelt sucker with flower trimmings

indicators.note: with simply adds one part alongside the others in sequence

blocks.note: an animal's pelt is its fur
a nit is a fool, someone easily taken in
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A fur coat edged with a bloodsucking parasite and floral decoration sounds like dubious fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword favourite for a river (a thing that flows); the Ure runs through North Yorkshire. 'Sucker' suggests a louse, but here it is a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture also means fittings and accessories, such as door handles and knobs, which are trimmings added to a structure.

clue.text: It provides lashings of hard copy in reverse

indicators.note: going in reverse means the word is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: a crib is a copied answer or a cheat sheet
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A printer turns out plenty of hard copy, but backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the copy is turned round; the hard abbreviation follows it. 'Lashings' suggests abundance but means whippings.
explanation.definitionFit: The birch is a bundle of twigs formerly used to flog offenders, so it delivers strokes of punishment.

clue.text: Give voice to soloist's first climax

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the opening letter of soloist
a peak is a high point or climax

explanation.surface: A singer reaches the high point of a solo performance.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus PEAK gives SPEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak is to utter or express something aloud in words, articulating thoughts verbally.

clue.text: Recipients of letter from American lassie chez Scotsman?

blocks.note: gal is an American word for a girl
chez means at the home of
Ian is a typical Scottish name; chez makes it at Ian's place

explanation.surface: An American girl staying at a Scotsman's house receives a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: GAL + AT + IANS: 'chez Scotsman' reads as 'at Ian's'. The letter is St Paul's epistle, not post.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Galatians in the New Testament was written by Paul to the Christian churches of Galatia.

clue.text: Diligent couple welcoming Lawrence to the States

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them inside, so one part holds another
to here means added on, so the last part simply follows

blocks.note: a duo is a pair
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia
the United States

explanation.surface: A hard-working pair host Lawrence on his trip to America.
explanation.walkthrough: DUO takes in TE to make DUTEO, then US: DUTEOUS. Lawrence is T. E. Lawrence, known by his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Duteous is an old word for dutiful, describing someone conscientious and obedient in carrying out obligations.

clue.text: 8 or amphibian's 18?

blocks.note: a toad is an amphibian, with the apostrophe s
tool is slang for the phallus, the answer to 18

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether a fungus belongs to a toad.
explanation.walkthrough: TOAD'S + TOOL gives TOADSTOOL; the question mark flags the slang sense of 18.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a mushroom, especially an inedible one, so it is a fungus, the answer to 8.

clue.text: Proviso about a plunderer

indicators.note: about means around, so one part wraps round the other

blocks.note: a rider is a condition added to a document
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal condition concerning a thief, as in a contract clause.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDER goes around A to give RAIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider attacks and loots, so the word is a synonym for someone who pillages.

clue.text: See 18
About to return drink of milk to the plant

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: ca is the abbreviation for circa, about
milk is delivered in pints

explanation.surface: Someone is about to take a drink of milk back to the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as a time phrase, but the words split: About is circa, and 'to return' turns the drink round.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a mint-family herb whose scent excites cats, hence its name.

clue.text: 3 generated by Lulu's mishap with Cupid

indicators.note: generated by means created from, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lulu suffers an embarrassing accident involving Cupid.
explanation.walkthrough: All sixteen letters of 'Lulu's mishap' and 'Cupid' rearrange into the fungus's Latin name, which means 'shameless phallus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phallus impudicus is the scientific name of the common stinkhorn, the answer to 3.

clue.text: Connoisseur entertaining quiet bartender

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so one part holds another

blocks.note: a taster judges wine or food
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A wine expert hosts a quiet barman.
explanation.walkthrough: TASTER takes in P: TAPSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an old word for someone who draws beer from the tap and serves customers in an inn.

clue.text: Flourish in hollow triumph before split

indicators.note: hollow means emptied, so only the outside letters stay
before places one part ahead of the next

blocks.note: the outside letters of triumph
to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: A victory feels empty ahead of a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: TH plus RIVE gives THRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to grow vigorously and prosper, so the verbs match.

clue.text: The remainder are sure to die horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests violent damage, so the letters are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim prophecy that the rest will meet a terrible end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The remainder are' reads as a plural subject, but 'are' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over after the rest has gone, the leftover part.

clue.text: Screen version of "The Perfume Dispenser"

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworked form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The film adaptation of a novel called The Perfume Dispenser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen version' suggests a film adaptation, but the quoted title is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is a vessel in which incense is burned, so it gives off scented smoke.

clue.text: 9's professional sinecure

blocks.note: first meaning: a comfortable armchair, an item of furniture, the answer to 9
second meaning: a cushy professorial post

explanation.walkthrough: A university chair is a professorship; one with no duties is an easy chair, a pun on the armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a well-upholstered armchair, and a chair is also an academic post, so a cushy one is a sinecure.

clue.text: Summit supplies key to period of peace

indicators.note: to here means added on, so the following part comes next

blocks.note: C is a musical key
a rest is a period of calm

explanation.surface: A summit meeting holds the key to a lasting peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a diplomatic meeting, but it is the definition: a top.
explanation.definitionFit: A crest is the top of a hill or wave, the highest point.

clue.text: Grass turned to Raffles

indicators.note: turned round means the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: sward is an expanse of grassy turf

explanation.surface: An informer becomes the gentleman thief Raffles, as in an old crime yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass looks like an informer and Raffles like the fictional burglar, but here raffles means lotteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Draws and raffles are both lotteries where tickets are pulled at random to award prizes.

clue.text: Do I resemble Thunderbirds, pal?

blocks.note: the question 'Am I...?'
from the catchphrase 'Thunderbirds are go!'

explanation.surface: A child asks a friend whether they look like a Thunderbirds puppet.
explanation.walkthrough: Thunderbirds was a 1960s British puppet TV series whose catchphrase was 'Thunderbirds are go!', so to resemble them is to be GO: AM I GO?
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, borrowed into English as a casual word for a mate.

clue.text: Second study of means of propagating 8

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
to pore over is to study closely

explanation.surface: A follow-up study looks into how fungi reproduce.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus PORE gives SPORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungi reproduce by releasing tiny single-celled reproductive bodies that disperse and grow into new organisms.

clue.text: Issue raised by union wanting official recognition

definitions.text: Issue raised by union wanting official recognition

blocks.clueFragment: Issue raised by union wanting official recognition
blocks.note: surface reading: a trade union pressing a claim for formal recognition by an employer

blocks.clueFragment: Issue raised by union wanting official recognition
blocks.note: setter's reading: offspring brought up from a relationship lacking the sanction of marriage

explanation.walkthrough: Issue means children, raised means brought up, and the union is a couple not legally wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A love child is a child born to parents who are not married, a union without legal standing.

clue.text: Connects with the deceased in residence

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other

blocks.note: res is the short form of residence
the late means the dead

explanation.surface: A medium makes contact with the dead at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate to something is to connect or be associated with it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Tree's source of minerals on land

blocks.note: the ash is a tree; the apostrophe s joins it to the next part
ore is rock from which minerals are extracted

explanation.surface: A tree's roots draw minerals from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: ASH plus ORE gives ASHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on dry ground rather than at sea, off the boat and on the beach.
